questions.prompt: What does this program print? (A linked list built at the front.)
questions.explain: Every new node becomes the head, so the list holds the squares in reverse order of insertion: 16, 9, 4, 1.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (One pass of bubble sort.)
questions.explain: A single pass swaps neighbours that are out of order and carries the largest value (5) to the end; the rest is only partly sorted.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Write numbers to a file, read them back.)
questions.explain: The file holds 10, 20, 30 and 40: four numbers adding up to 100.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Walking a string with a pointer.)
questions.explain: Subtracting 32 turns a lower-case ASCII letter into the upper-case one; the comma becomes a semicolon and the space is unchanged.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Recursion that prints before and after.)
questions.explain: Each call prints its `n` before the recursive call (going down: 3 2 1) and again after it returns (coming back: 1 2 3).

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (An array of structs modified through pointers.)
questions.explain: `&t[0]` and `t + 1` are both pointers to elements of the array, so `add` changes the originals: ann 1 + 4 and bob 5 + 1.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (qsort with a comparison function.)
questions.explain: The comparison returns `b - a`, so larger numbers sort first: descending order.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Character classes from <ctype.h>.)
questions.explain: Upper-case letters: `C` and `F` (2). Digits: `9` and `9` (2). Spaces: two. The `!` and the lower-case letters are not counted.

questions.prompt: What is the bug in this loop that copies `src` into `dst`?
questions.explain: The loop stops when `*src` is `'\0'` BEFORE copying it. After the loop `dst[i]` must be set to `'\0'` (or use `strcpy`).
options: It never copies the terminating '\0', so `dst` is not a valid string
It copies one character too many
It reads past the end of dst
option_notes: It copies one too few (the terminator).
It writes up to the length of src.

questions.prompt: Which of these are the most common causes of a segmentation fault?
questions.explain: All three access memory the program must not touch. A wrong printf format is also undefined behaviour but is far less likely to crash.
options: Dereferencing a NULL or uninitialised pointer
Writing past the end of an array
Printing with the wrong format using printf
option_notes: Usually prints garbage rather than crashing (but it is a bug).

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Binary search in a sorted array.)
questions.explain: `bsearch` returns a pointer to the matching element; subtracting the start of the array gives its index, 3.

questions.prompt: A program calls `srand(42)` at the start and then `rand()` several times. If you run it twice, what do you get?
questions.explain: `rand` is a deterministic generator: the same seed gives the same numbers. Seed it once with something that changes, such as `time(NULL)`, for varying results.
option_notes: Only if you seed with a changing value.
42 is the seed, not the result.

questions.explain: It is a `time_t` count of seconds; convert it with `localtime` or `strftime`. For CPU time use `clock()` divided by `CLOCKS_PER_SEC`.
options: The number of seconds since January 1, 1970 (the Epoch)
The CPU time of the program

questions.explain: `system` starts a shell (`sh -c`), runs the command and returns its exit status. Never build the command from untrusted input.
options: Runs the command in a shell, waits for it, and returns its status
Lists the files into a string
option_notes: Output goes to the terminal, not into a variable.

questions.prompt: How do you read the manual page of the system call `open`, and not of the shell command with the same name?
questions.explain: Section 2 holds system calls, section 3 library functions and section 1 commands: `man 2 open`, `man 3 printf`.
option_notes: The section number comes before the name.
The section is given as a plain number.

questions.prompt: `return 3;` at the end of `main` is equivalent to which call?
questions.explain: Returning from `main` ends the program with that exit status, just like `exit`. The shell shows it in `$?`.
